newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German June BME/Reuters PMI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German June BME/Reuters PMI data.

text.p: Following are a series of analysts' reactions to the BME/Reuters purchasing managers' index for June which showed that the index fell to a seasonally adjusted level of 56.83 compared with 57.77 in May.
On an unadjusted basis, the index eased to 56.62 from 57.42.

CHRIS WILLIAMSON, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT NTC RESEARCH, THE COMPANY WHICH COMPILES THE INDEX : "It's really too small a movement to put much emphasis on. The output in new orders growth is very strong at the moment."

UWE ANGENENDT, BHF BANK - "We saw several months of increase in the PMI and the sight decline in June is not a turaround. In May we will see stronger production and order figures and a slight decline in June in these figures.

"All in all we will see a stronger second quarter than the first quarter...at least a one percent increase in second quarter. (That means) the German economy is on a good track to reach 2.5 percent growth, which is the government expectation."

"We have higher import prices and I think this is attributed to the price component in this PMI index. But I do not think the price pressure is dangerous. We have very low unit labour costs in Germany and wage settlements. There is no reason to expect an acceleration in prices.
"Some raw materials are expensive at the beginning of the year but I do not think this is very dangerous.

"We have not seen up to now spillover effects on domestic demand. We do not really expect further improvement in the labour market and that is reflected in the PMI index. The labour index has deteriorated further and that is the big problem for the German economy at the time being.
"We expect only a slight improvement in seasonally-adjsuted German job figures.

"I think the process will continue. There are a lot of uncertainties in the market. We have the risks of further strengths in economic indicators in the UK and the USA and that a rate hike is possible. I think that will have a positive impact on the dollar."

MATHIAS HAFFNER, ECONOMIST AT BZW IN FRANKFURT: "Indeed the indications that Germany is on a relatively stable growth path have increased over the last few months. The release of the PMI is not a contradiction to that view.
"The increase in the price index is a reflection of a very natural development at this point of the cycle. We have seen volume order growth growing very rapidly.
"The problems are far from over and I am not sure we have seen the peak in unemployment.
"I find it interesting to note that the recent dollar strength since Monday afternoon is due more to comments about a delay (in EMU) from Mr. Stoiber rather than worries about a softer euro."
/////The comments were taken from an instant analysis of the figures which ran on Reuters Financial Television.
